title: Mathias et Camille au café  (Mathias and Camille at the Café)

segments.t: Mathias meets his secret daughter Camille at a quiet cafe across town. After his wife Catherine kicked him out for his years of lies, Mathias wants to come clean to everyone at ASK. However, Camille is horrified by the prospect of being exposed. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Tu es sûre d'avoir assez mangé?
Alors, tu as quelque chose à me dire.
J'ai fait du mal en cachant la vérité pendant des années.
Catherine m'a mis à la porte.
Elle pense que je suis un menteur.
Je veux réparer ça et dire la vérité.
Je veux dire à tout le monde que tu es ma fille.
À l'agence? Mais maintenant j'ai peur.
Peur de quoi, Camille?
J'ai peur de perdre la confiance de mes collègues.
Tu crois qu'Andréa veut de ta fille comme assistante?
Hervé et Noémie sont mes amis maintenant.
Ils vont penser que je suis une menteuse.
Je suis très heureuse ici, je ne veux pas gâcher ça.
Let's examine how Mathias and Camille discuss their hidden family secret.
Tu es sûre d'avoir assez mangé?
'Are you sure you have eaten enough?' Mathias shows fatherly care using the compound past infinitive.
Alors, tu as quelque chose à me dire.
'So, you have something to tell me.' Camille prompts him directly with an indefinite pronoun construction.
J'ai fait du mal en cachant la vérité pendant des années.
'I caused harm by hiding the truth for years.' A gerund form expressing the continuous cause of distress.
Catherine m'a mis à la porte.
'Catherine threw me out.' An idiomatic past expression literally meaning put to the door.
Elle pense que je suis un menteur.
'She thinks I am a liar.' A verb of opinion governing a second part of the sentence with a predicate noun.
Je veux réparer ça et dire la vérité.
'I want to fix that and tell the truth.' Two infinitives joined by a connecting word after a modal verb.
Je veux dire à tout le monde que tu es ma fille.
'I want to tell everyone that you are my daughter.' Mathias states his wish to acknowledge his child publicly.
À l'agence? Mais maintenant j'ai peur.
'At the agency? But now I am afraid.' Camille reacts with shock followed by an expression of fear.
Peur de quoi, Camille?
'Afraid of what, Camille?' Mathias asks for clarification with a linking word and question word.
J'ai peur de perdre la confiance de mes collègues.
'I am afraid of losing the trust of my colleagues.' The key word here means 'I have', paired with 'coworkers' to make the point clear.
Tu crois qu'Andréa veut de ta fille comme assistante?
'Do you think Andréa wants your daughter as an assistant?' A question highlighting professional vulnerability.
Hervé et Noémie sont mes amis maintenant.
'Hervé and Noémie are my friends now.' Camille describes her newly built personal and professional bonds.
Ils vont penser que je suis une menteuse.
'They will think that I am a liar.' The near-future tense expressing Camille's fear of social rejection.
Je suis très heureuse ici, je ne veux pas gâcher ça.
'I am very happy here, I do not want to ruin that.' A heartfelt appeal to preserve her current happiness. Now let's listen to their conversation at the cafe again without interruptions.

Camille desperately wants to protect her independent life at the agency. Mathias agrees to keep quiet for now, but keeping such a major secret is never easy. Until next time.
À demain!
